strategy.summary: Reproduce PR #20405 by building scipy at buggy commit a24f7847e8cc with the developer's regression test applied, then running that single test. On the buggy revision cephes.yn(500, 1) returns NaN, so the exact equality to -np.inf fails. On the fixed revision the loop stops once an becomes infinite and the test passes.

pinned_because: numpy<2: era-inferred from PR date 2024-04-08; the evidence does not document this constraint

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy a24f7847e8cc the test fails with AssertionError because cephes.yn(500, 1) is NaN and NaN == -inf is False. On the fixed revision the test passes because cephes.yn(500, 1) returns -inf exactly.
risks: The reproducing test exercises only cephes.yn. It does not exercise the Amos yv path, so passing it does not show the amos.h unk2 change is correct; the existing yv(300,1) and yv(300,1+0j) checks in test_basic.py are needed for that.
The NaN comes from the recurrence after overflow, so it depends on IEEE arithmetic behaviour. Builds with -ffast-math or other non-IEEE flags may not reproduce it.
Target platform (architecture, OS, libm) is not stated in the evidence, so the transition is assumed on common x86_64 Linux; platform-specific behaviour is unverified.
Numpy 2.x may break the 2024-era build. The numpy<2 pin is era-inferred, not documented.
Editable build of scipy from source is slow and needs a working C/C++ toolchain and meson; build failure would prevent any transition check.
Confirm the checkout is the buggy parent commit and not the fixed one, or the test will pass on both sides and the transition is lost.

oracle.reference_source: developer test assertion (observed == -np.inf) and Wolfram BesselY per PR discussion
oracle.why: The test uses exact equality with -inf and no tolerance, so the oracle is exact.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion sees cephes.yn(500, 1) = NaN on the buggy revision. NaN == -inf is False, so AssertionError is raised because the loop condition does not stop when an becomes infinite and later iterations produce NaN.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed loop condition while (k < n && isfinite(an)) stops once an is infinite, so the function returns -inf and the equality holds exactly.
